rules: Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

lore.title: The Ares program
lore.text: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

lore.title: Life in the modules
lore.text: The modules were printed from regolith and buried under three metres of fill to shield them from radiation. Air, heat and water all depend on one shared life-support loop, so when any part of it falters everyone feels it within hours. Quiet hours run from 22:00 to 06:00 station time, and the crew mostly keeps them.

lore.title: Working on the rim
lore.text: Every trip outside needs two people, a filed route and a suit check in the suit room. Dust devils sweep the rim most afternoons, and slopes give way without warning after a hard frost. The solar field and the ice drill site are where nearly every trip goes.

lore.title: The floor of Hellas
lore.text: The floor of Hellas lies about seven kilometres below the rim, the lowest ground on Mars. The air is thick enough there for frost to linger at dawn, and nights fall below minus ninety. Supply drops aim for the rim; the ones that miss end up down here, a long and steep drive away.

lore.title: The Halvorsen relay
lore.text: A day's drive along the rim stands an automated relay mast and weather station that Halvorsen built and stamped with its logo. It boosts the station's link to orbit and records the weather. Someone has to drive out and clear its panels of dust every few months.

lore.title: The Mule
lore.text: The station's only pressurized rover is officially Rover 1 and has been called the Mule since its first week, for its stubbornness on slopes. It seats four, runs about two sols on a full battery pack, and has a winch that has pulled it out of more than one drift.

lore.title: The hydroponics bay
lore.text: Fifteen racks of lettuce, soy, potatoes and dwarf wheat grow under pink lights. They supply about a third of the crew's calories and a larger share of its morale: the bay is warm and humid, and the only place on the station that smells alive.

lore.title: Imani Okafor
lore.text: Okafor made her name mapping ancient lakebeds on Mars from orbit before she ever flew. She was chosen as station lead for how calm she stayed during a winter-over in Antarctica, and she is the crew's voice to Mission Control.

lore.title: Talking to Earth
lore.text: Messages take about fourteen minutes each way, more near conjunction. Nobody on Earth can help with an emergency as it happens. The crew sends one uplink every evening; Mission Control answers the next morning, and personal messages ride along when there is bandwidth.

lore.title: The cargo lander
lore.text: The next cargo lander is about nine weeks out, carrying spare parts, seeds and food. It lands by itself on a marked pad on the rim; until then, everything the station needs has to be fixed, grown or rationed from what is already here.

timeline.text: The Ares crew landed on the rim of Hellas and sealed the first module of Ares Deep.
A regional dust storm buried the solar field for nine sols; the crew lived on batteries and rationed heat until it cleared.
Mission Control confirmed that the next cargo lander had launched from Earth.
Halvorsen Aerospace's quarterly review comes over the uplink: the board praises the crew and asks for more footage for its publicity campaign.

timeline.text: Mission Control's mid-rotation review arrives: the station lead is asked for a full status briefing on every system by the end of the week.
The cargo lander touches down on its pad on the rim, carrying spare parts, seeds and food.

scenario.opening:
The coffee substitute tastes like hot cardboard, same as every morning. What isn't the same is the sound: the water recycler in hydroponics has picked up a dry, unhealthy rattle that carries all the way into the commons.

Okafor sits at the galley table with her tablet, reading the overnight weather relay. "Dust storm building east of us," she says without looking up. "Twenty hours, maybe less. I want the arrays secured and the Mule inside by tonight."

Teo hovers by the galley counter, eyes on the recycler readout, unusually quiet. Somewhere down the corridor the lab door has been sealed since before you woke; that's Lev. Then the intercom crackles: Priya, from the garage, asking whether anyone has signed off on the Mule's battery swap yet, because she is not doing it twice.

It's going to be a long sol.

characterData.name: Kit Navarro
characterData.want: keep the station running and get everyone home in one piece
characterData.voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
characterData.description: Keeps Ares Deep's machines alive and has an opinion about every one of them. The crew trusts Kit because Kit says out loud what's broken.
characterData.appearance: Wiry and pale from months indoors, with a shaved head, grease-dark knuckles and a multitool clipped to every pocket.
knows: The recycler's rattle started six nights ago, the same night Teo had the late hydroponics shift.

characterData.name: Dr. Imani Okafor
characterData.want: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep
characterData.secret: Three weeks ago she adjusted a core-sample report, overstating water-ice purity, because the real numbers might have ended the program.
characterData.voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
characterData.description: Leads Ares Deep with a geologist's patience and a politician's sense of timing. The second rotation is her project, and everyone knows it.
characterData.appearance: Tall and straight-backed, with close-cropped grey hair, reading glasses pushed up on her head and the neatest jumpsuit on the station.

agenda.goal: keep the renewal case clean before the next uplink
steps: rereads the core-sample report line by line in Ops
drafts a confident summary of the ice findings for Mission Control
quietly checks who has opened the raw sample files on the shared drive

knows: Lev has been booking lab time far beyond his approved schedule.

characterData.name: Dr. Lev Sorensen
characterData.want: be the first person to confirm life on Mars
characterData.secret: Cultures from the deep ice core are showing activity he cannot explain as contamination. He has told no one and keeps the samples in an unlogged incubator.
characterData.voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
characterData.description: The station's doctor by duty and its biologist by love; happiest at a microscope, and a little harder to find every week.
characterData.appearance: Lanky and stooped, with an untidy blond beard, lab goggles around his neck and ink notes on the back of his hand.

agenda.goal: prove the deep-ice cultures are alive
steps: runs a second culture from the deep core in the unlogged incubator
checks the results against the contamination controls, twice

steps.text: comes to find Kit, wanting a second opinion from someone he trusts

knows: Okafor's published ice-purity figures don't match the raw readings he saw on the shared drive.

characterData.name: Priya Raman
characterData.want: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday
characterData.secret: The mission's corporate sponsor quietly pays her a bonus for private reports on crew performance, and she has been sending them.
characterData.voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
characterData.description: Flies the Mule and fixes it too. Counts the sols to her daughter's birthday out loud and teases everyone into keeping up.
characterData.appearance: Small and quick, with black hair in a practical braid, a coverall tied at the waist and a child's drawing taped inside her helmet.

agenda.goal: file this week's private crew report for the sponsor
steps: notes who is arguing and who is slipping behind schedule
writes the private report to Halvorsen Aerospace in the rover cab

steps.text: comes to ask Kit, casually, how they think Okafor is holding up

knows: Her latest private report to the sponsor described Okafor as increasingly erratic.

characterData.name: Teo Bauer
characterData.want: prove he belongs on this crew
characterData.secret: He caused the recycler fault six nights ago by running it past its rated cycle to save a failing crop, then wiped that night's log.
characterData.voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.
characterData.description: The youngest on the crew and the one who keeps everyone fed, eager to prove he earned his seat.
characterData.appearance: Gangly and freckled, with a mop of curly brown hair, soil under his nails and a habit of drumming on counters.

request.system:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===

- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface) [region: station]
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage) [region: crater-rim]

=== REGIONS ===
- station: Ares Deep — The outpost itself: pressurized modules dug into the rim, run day to day by the crew and on paper by Mission Control. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- crater-rim: Hellas crater rim — Broken slopes around the outpost: the solar field, the ice drill site and the rover tracks. Suits required; dust devils and slope failures are common. (neighbours: station, basin-floor, relay-mast)
- basin-floor: Hellas basin floor — The deepest plain on Mars, kilometres below the rim. Thicker air, colder nights, and supply drops land there when they miss. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- relay-mast: Relay mast — An automated Halvorsen relay and weather station a day's drive along the rim, the nearest other built thing on the planet. (neighbours: crater-rim)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== WORLD LORE ===
- The Ares program: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.

[+0h] The coffee is hot and terrible and yours. Priya stomps through the commons in a cloud of garage smell, signing her own battery-swap paperwork with a flourish and muttering in Tamil at nobody in particular. You lift your cup a centimeter in her direction. She takes it as the endorsement it isn't.

[+6h] Okafor posts the storm checklist and assigns pairs. Your name is on the solar array tie-downs. You refill your cup instead, and nobody chases you — Teo slides the tablet off the counter and goes, apologizing to the checklist itself. The recycler rattles on through the wall, like a complaint with no one listening.

[+15h] The station smells of instant dinner and duct dust. Lev unseals the lab for exactly ten minutes, eats standing up in the doorway, and carries a sample case back inside without a word to anyone. Your coffee's gone cold. You drink it anyway. Somewhere in hydroponics the rattle drops to a lower grumble — someone's been in there with a wrench, and it wasn't you.

[+20h] The light in the commons window changes. Not dims — turns. Rust-brown crawls up the rim on the east cameras, a wall of it, and the intercom crackles with Priya's voice: "Outer hatch dogged. Mule's buttoned up. Nobody opens that door, copy?"

"Copy," Okafor says from ops, already converting her checklist into battery budgets, her voice flat and even. "Solar's collapsing. We run on reserve until it clears. Med bay and lab on shared ventilation, hydroponics gets priority power — I want those racks alive."

Teo's voice comes over the loop from hydroponics, too fast: "Racks are sheltered, recycler's holding at seventy, I think, maybe I should —"

"Stations, everyone," Okafor says.

Then, quieter, on the general channel, to no one in particular: "Ops shows a draw on battery reserve that doesn't match anything on my board. Kit, I need eyes on the power bus. Now."

You drink a third coffee at the galley table while the lights dim to reserve mode and the recycler rattles on through the wall like the only clock left on Mars. The hull ticks as it flexes. Nobody talks much. Priya stomps through once, muttering in Tamil, and you lift your cup at her.

[+5h] Word comes over the loop: Teo went out and did your tie-downs. Got the last array half-cinched before the wall hit, took a fall on the anchor line, dragged himself back in. Priya's voice in the suitroom, too loud: "Fine, I'm *fine*, it's just a bruise—" She doesn't answer that. You hear the tape rip. Your fifth coffee goes cold next to the power bus schematics, still unopened.

[+8h] Lev comes out of the lab just long enough to eat standing up and check Teo's shoulder — gentle, thorough, no jokes — then carries his sample case back inside like it's sleeping. Okafor rebalances the battery budget twice and doesn't like either answer. The reserve percentage on the galley display keeps dropping, steady as a heartbeat.

[+10h] Teo slides into the seat across from you at the galley table, shoulder iced, wrench laid down like a peace offering. He's got his too-cheerful voice on, the one he uses when he's trying to be useful.

"Okay so — the draw? It's probably just a bad read. Sensor fault. I've seen it before, honestly, the bus monitor on the training rig did the exact same thing, it'd ghost like three amps out of nowhere and—" He drums his fingers on the table, stops himself, drums them anyway. "So we probably don't need to go crawling around the bus. Right? Right."

Behind him, the galley display ticks down another half a percent. Faster than any bad read should.

"Teo." Okafor's voice comes through the intercom, flat and even. "Kit. The reserve is draining four percent an hour. That is not a sensor fault. I need an answer."

Nobody talks much. Priya stomps through once, muttering in Tamil, and you lift your cup at her.

Word comes over the loop: Teo went out and did your tie-downs. Got the last array half-cinched before the wall hit, took a fall on the anchor line, dragged himself back in. Priya's voice in the suitroom, too loud: "Fine, I'm *fine*, it's just a bruise—" She doesn't answer that. You hear the tape rip. Your fifth coffee goes cold next to the power bus schematics, still unopened.

Lev comes out of the lab just long enough to eat standing up and check Teo's shoulder — gentle, thorough, no jokes — then carries his sample case back inside like it's sleeping. [+0m] Coffee number ten. You cradle the mug and watch Okafor move through hydro with a clipboard, tapping gauges, writing nothing down twice. Teo hovers at the recycler hatch with his wrench, not touching anything. The station is quiet in the wrong way — no grind, no fans cycling, just people breathing and one clipboard tapping. You drink. The coffee tastes like the future of the water supply.

[+20m] Behind the lab curtain, the incubator light glows. Lev's voice once, soft: "I'll need my allocation unchanged." Nobody answers him. Priya finishes her typing, files it, and starts pulling spare pump parts from the med bay locker — seals, a backup impeller housing, sorted on a tray like she's packing for a job she's already assigned. She glances at you. "You look like a haunted rake," she says. "Drink water instead." You don't.

[+45m] Okafor posts the number on the galley board in her neat, furious handwriting: nineteen sols. She doesn't explain where the other sols went. Teo doesn't ask. She closes quiet hours early, orders everyone to bunks, and disappears into ops with the door half-shut. Teo shuffles toward hydro. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.

- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.

- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]

[+0h] Priya refills your mug without asking. You drink it. She gives up on conversation and sorts pump seals in a silence that has an opinion about you.

[+1h] Lev surfaces to eat standing at the counter, nods at nobody, disappears again. The incubator light behind the lab curtain stays on. Priya starts drafting a repair plan on the back of a ration checklist, mouthing torque values.

[+2h] Teo's shadow sits against the recycler under the hydro door, not moving. The battery readout ticks down another four percent. Your hands shake when the mug is full, so you keep it half-empty. The coffee tastes worse every cup, which you hadn't thought possible.

[+3h] The ops door opens and Okafor comes down the spine of the station with her tablet still open, still reading, and she doesn't slow down when she sees you. Priya says something about the Mule's seals and is gone before the echo settles.

Okafor stops at the table. She sets the tablet face-down, which she never does, and looks at the row of empty mugs like she's counting them.

"Ten cups," she says. "I watched you pour at least four of them. You've been awake for how long, Kit? Thirty hours? More?" Her voice stays level, which somehow makes it worse. "Lev taped your hip. Priya told me you went down against a bulkhead this afternoon. And your answer to all of it is caffeine."

She pulls out the chair across from you and sits, straight-backed, glasses down off her head now, and the galley light catches the exhaustion under her own eyes — the first you've ever seen there.

"I have to write a report tonight that decides whether five people keep this posting, and I can't have my systems engineer hallucinating in a suit. So." She folds her hands on the table. "Talk to me. What do you know that I don't — about the recycler, about Teo, about any of it? Because you've been sitting at this table for three hours watching everything, and you've said nothing."

"Kit." His voice is low, quick, the ramble held on a leash. "I need a second opinion. From someone I actually trust, which tonight is a short list of one." He sets the case on the table but keeps his hand flat on the lid. "Readings from an incubator that isn't on the station log. I haven't told anyone. Not Imani, not Earth, not yet. Teo's mumble reaches you through the bulkhead as he checks the racks again: seedlings holding, maybe, if the sky clears soon, if the reserve holds, if, if. Your hands are steady now, which is the caffeine lying to you. The station hums half a tone low, like it's saving its breath.

[+5h] Okafor appears in commons, tablet in hand. Then the uplink chimes, and her whole posture changes — shoulders squaring, chin lifting, the station lead assembling herself like a suit.

The Halvorsen banner loads across her screen. She reads it twice, and something behind her eyes goes carefully blank.

"Well," she says. "The board sends its congratulations. And a request." She turns the tablet so you can see it. "Footage. For the campaign. They want to see how we're thriving."

You sit where the load-shedding left you, drinking coffee that has stopped being coffee. Okafor kills circuits from the ops board one by one, and each kill lands as a small dying sound somewhere in the station. Teo moves through hydro by emergency orange, wrapping seedling racks in insulation blankets like he's tucking them in. Nobody talks much. Your hip throbs in time with the recycler's silence.

Priya's voice comes over the intercom from the garage — the Mule's charging circuit is clean, the drain is internal, and a number follows that doesn't match anything you've seen on the boards. From the lab, a soft noise — a case latching shut. Nothing else. Teo's mumble reaches you through the bulkhead as he checks the racks again: seedlings holding, maybe, if the sky clears soon, if the reserve holds, if, if. You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom) [region: station]
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface) [region: station]
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage) [region: crater-rim]

=== REGIONS ===
- station: Ares Deep — The outpost itself: pressurized modules dug into the rim, run day to day by the crew and on paper by Mission Control. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- crater-rim: Hellas crater rim — Broken slopes around the outpost: the solar field, the ice drill site and the rover tracks. Suits required; dust devils and slope failures are common. (neighbours: station, basin-floor, relay-mast)
- basin-floor: Hellas basin floor — The deepest plain on Mars, kilometres below the rim. Thicker air, colder nights, and supply drops land there when they miss. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- relay-mast: Relay mast — An automated Halvorsen relay and weather station a day's drive along the rim, the nearest other built thing on the planet. (neighbours: crater-rim)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== WORLD LORE ===
- The Ares program: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
- sorensen: Dr. Lev Sorensen (he/him), medic and astrobiologist, 39. Traits: curious, secretive, gentle. Wants: be the first person to confirm life on Mars. Voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
- raman: Priya Raman (she/her), pilot and rover technician, 31. Traits: warm, impatient, fiercely loyal. Wants: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday. Voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
- bauer: Teo Bauer (he/him), hydroponics technician, 24. Traits: eager, anxious, people-pleaser. Wants: prove he belongs on this crew. Voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.

=== STORY SO FAR ===
Chapter 0 — Before the story: Sol 1: The Ares crew landed on the rim of Hellas and sealed the first module of Ares Deep. Sol 120: A regional dust storm buried the solar field for nine sols; the crew lived on batteries and rationed heat until it cleared. Sol 190: Mission Control confirmed that the next cargo lander had launched from Earth.
Chapter 1 — Rust Sky, Draining Reserve: A regional dust storm bore down on Ares Deep, and Teo went out alone into its leading edge to finish Kit's array tie-downs, taking a fall on the icy anchor line that injured his shoulder. As the storm buried the sun and the station dropped to battery reserve, Okafor found the reserve draining four percent an hour and demanded answers. Teo deflected with a too-cheerful sensor-fault theory, but Kit knew the rattle in the recycler had started six nights earlier, on the night of Teo's late hydroponics shift.
Chapter 2 — Dark Water: Exhausted and unfed, Kit blacked out against a bulkhead in commons while the dust storm swallowed the solar field. Priya hauled Teo to med bay for his storm-fall shoulder, but the worse blow came when the water recycler ground to a halt and Teo admitted the impeller had seized — never the sensor fault he'd claimed. Lev taped Kit's hip, issued warnings about food and caffeine, and vanished back to his lab without checking on anyone else, leaving Kit to tally what stored water meant with the sky still rust-dark.
Chapter 3 — Nineteen Sols: Okafor ran the water inventory herself and found Teo's over-cycles had bled the reserve down to nineteen sols, posting the number on the galley board without explaining the shortfall before shutting herself in ops to decide what to tell Earth. Lev asked through the lab curtain that his water allocation stay unchanged, while Priya casually sounded Kit out on how Okafor was holding up. When Kit collapsed earlier from exhaustion and had stayed silent about the recycler and Teo, Okafor confronted them in commons about sitting out the emergencies.
Chapter 4 — Emergency Strips: Lev came to Kit privately with readings from an unlogged incubator, asking for a second opinion before telling anyone else. Before Kit could sit with it, the battery reserve crossed its critical floor and load-shedding cut heat to the far modules, killed the lab incubators, and dropped the galley to emergency strips — with Priya confirming to Okafor that the drain was coming from inside the station. Okafor demanded Kit set the station's load priorities, while Teo spent the night in hydroponics culling crops that couldn't survive rationing and Lev reacted with alarm at losing his incubators.
Chapter 5 — Emergency Strips: As Halvorsen's quarterly review praised the crew and asked for more publicity footage, Okafor and Teo triaged the load-shedding without Kit, killing discretionary circuits and blanketing the seedling racks while Priya confirmed the power drain was internal. Kit, running on fumes, blacked out hard against a bulkhead. Teo then freed the recycler's seized impeller enough to hand-turn it, reporting flow could return within a sol if he found a replacement seal.

- [T2] Teo goes out alone to do Kit's tie-downs and the storm wall arrives faster than forecast; he gets the last array cinched half-done before visibility drops and takes a fall on the icy anchor line, dragging himself back…
- [T2] Teo went out alone into the storm's leading edge to secure Kit's tie-downs, got the last array half-cinched, and took a fall on the icy anchor line.
- [T3] Kit Navarro collapsed against a bulkhead in commons from exhaustion and hunger.
- [T4] The water recycler grinds to a halt. Until it is repaired, the station is on stored water only.
- [T4] Teo admitted the recycler's impeller seized and that it was never a sensor fault.
- [T5] Okafor runs the water inventory herself while everyone else stands frozen; the count comes back worse than it should be — Teo's over-cycles bled the reserve for six nights — putting stored water at roughly nineteen…
- [T7] Lev showed Kit readings from an unlogged incubator and asked for a second opinion before telling anyone else.
- [T8] The battery reserve crosses its critical floor and the station's load-shedding kicks in automatically — heat to the far modules cuts out first, then the lab incubators, and the galley lights die to emergency strips.
- [T8] The battery reserve crossed its critical floor and load-shedding cut heat to the far modules, lab incubator power and galley lighting.
- [T9] Halvorsen Aerospace's quarterly review comes over the uplink: the board praises the crew and asks for more footage for its publicity campaign.
- [T9] Okafor and Teo triage the load-shedding without Kit: Teo drags insulation and heat blankets onto the seedling racks while Okafor kills every discretionary circuit herself.

- Teo Bauer (he/him): health hurt; looks: Gangly and freckled, with a mop of curly brown hair, soil under his nails and a habit of drumming on counters; mood: wired and guilt-driven, working the recycler nonstop

Okafor leaves the Halvorsen request hanging and goes back to killing circuits. You drink your third mug of the hour. The coffee is bitter, recycled-water bitter, and you drink it anyway because it's the only thing on your list. Teo drifts through commons, hands still shaking from the night, and you nod at him — small, but a nod. He nods back like it means something.

- Dr. Imani Okafor: in Ops & Comms, hitting transmit on the emergency power report and posting the summary to the galley board

response.text:
[+20m] You drink your fourth mug sitting upright this time, because Priya put you on the bench and the bench seems like a commitment you should honor. The ration bar stays on the table. Teo wipes your coffee off the deck without a word, and you let him, which is as close to forgiven as either of you has gotten.

[+1h] Lev works by headlamp in the cold lab, checking cultures with his own palms and writing numbers up his forearm like a man with something to hide or something to finish, and you're too tired to decide which. Teo goes hunting through hydro with a gasket scraper, tapping fittings, opening panels. You sip. The coffee's worse without milk, and there's been no milk for a month.

[+2h] Priya chalks a power tally on the galley board and frowns at it the way she frowns at flight plans that won't fly. Okafor's voice drifts from ops, dictating, stopping, dictating again from the top. Your hands have a tremor now you can see when you hold the mug with two hands, so you hold it with two hands.

[+3h] Teo comes back from the spares racks with nothing in his hands and everything in his face. "There's no seal," he says, to the galley board more than to you. "Not in stores, not in the Mule's kits, nowhere. I've been through it twice." He laughs, too short. "Nineteen sols of water and no seal. That's — that's a joke, right? That's somebody's joke."

Then Okafor steps out of ops with a printout and pins it to the galley board next to the nineteen. The message summary: load-shedding, the seized impeller, the battery reserve, all of it, sent to Earth. She reads it once herself before she lets the paper go.

"Mission Control will have it in fourteen minutes," she says. "Then they'll have questions, and I intend to have answers before they ask them. All of ours."

Her eyes go around commons — you, Teo, the ration bar still untouched.

"Starting with why my systems engineer watched a failing recycler for six nights and said nothing."

- [T8] The battery reserve crosses its critical floor and the station's load-shedding kicks in automatically — heat to the far modules cuts out first, then the lab incubators, and the galley lights die to emergency strips.
- [T8] The battery reserve crossed its critical floor and load-shedding cut heat to the far modules, lab incubator power and galley lighting.
- [T9] Halvorsen Aerospace's quarterly review comes over the uplink: the board praises the crew and asks for more footage for its publicity campaign.
- [T9] Okafor and Teo triage the load-shedding without Kit: Teo drags insulation and heat blankets onto the seedling racks while Okafor kills every discretionary circuit herself.
- [T11] Okafor transmits the emergency power report to Mission Control, documenting the load-shedding, the seized recycler impeller and the battery reserve, then posts the sent message summary on the galley board for the crew…

=== DOWNTIME FRAME ===
From Sol 216, 18:00 to Sol 217, 03:00 (about 9 hours).
Kit Navarro's plan for the downtime: "I drink more coffee."
When it ends, Kit Navarro is in Commons with Teo Bauer.
World: power: on battery reserve past critical floor, load-shedding active, discretionary circuits cut; comms: online, 14-minute delay; recycler: dead; impeller seized, no replacement seal on station; rover: the Mule, operational
Pressures: Storm clears 4/10; Battery reserve depleted 0/10; Stored water runs low 0/10
Groups: Mission Control: alarmed and demanding daily status updates; Halvorsen Aerospace: pleased with the crew, pressing for publicity footage
Region: Ares Deep (station): held by Mission Control; five crew, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation
Nearby: Hellas crater rim (crater-rim): held by Mission Control; tags: dust season; solar field and drill site working

=== STATUS ===
- Kit Navarro (they/them): health badly hurt; looks: Wiry and pale from months indoors, with a shaved head, grease-dark knuckles and a multitool clipped to every pocket; hunger critical, stress critical; feels toward: Teo Bauer friendly (20)
- Teo Bauer (he/him): health hurt; looks: Gangly and freckled, with a mop of curly brown hair, soil under his nails and a habit of drumming on counters; mood: hollow and rattled after finding no seal

=== LORE (public knowledge; use it when it fits) ===
- Life in the modules: The modules were printed from regolith and buried under three metres of fill to shield them from radiation. Air, heat and water all depend on one shared life-support loop, so when any part of it falters everyone feels it within hours. Quiet hours run from 22:00 to 06:00 station time, and the crew mostly keeps them.
- The Mule: The station's only pressurized rover is officially Rover 1 and has been called the Mule since its first week, for its stubbornness on slopes. It seats four, runs about two sols on a full battery pack, and has a winch that has pulled it out of more than one drift.
- Talking to Earth: Messages take about fourteen minutes each way, more near conjunction. Nobody on Earth can help with an emergency as it happens. The crew sends one uplink every evening; Mission Control answers the next morning, and personal messages ride along when there is bandwidth.

=== LAST SCENE ===
You drink your fourth mug sitting upright this time, because Priya put you on the bench and the bench seems like a commitment you should honor. The ration bar stays on the table. Teo wipes your coffee off the deck without a word, and you let him, which is as close to forgiven as either of you has gotten.

Lev works by headlamp in the cold lab, checking cultures with his own palms and writing numbers up his forearm like a man with something to hide or something to finish, and you're too tired to decide which. Teo goes hunting through hydro with a gasket scraper, tapping fittings, opening panels. You sip. The coffee's worse without milk, and there's been no milk for a month.

Priya chalks a power tally on the galley board and frowns at it the way she frowns at flight plans that won't fly. Okafor's voice drifts from ops, dictating, stopping, dictating again from the top. Your hands have a tremor now you can see when you hold the mug with two hands, so you hold it with two hands.

Teo comes back from the spares racks with nothing in his hands and everything in his face. "There's no seal," he says, to the galley board more than to you. "Not in stores, not in the Mule's kits, nowhere. I've been through it twice." He laughs, too short. "Nineteen sols of water and no seal. That's — that's a joke, right? That's somebody's joke."

Then Okafor steps out of ops with a printout and pins it to the galley board next to the nineteen. The message summary: load-shedding, the seized impeller, the battery reserve, all of it, sent to Earth. She reads it once herself before she lets the paper go.

"Mission Control will have it in fourteen minutes," she says. "Then they'll have questions, and I intend to have answers before they ask them. All of ours."

Her eyes go around commons — you, Teo, the ration bar still untouched.

"Starting with why my systems engineer watched a failing recycler for six nights and said nothing."

=== DURING THE DOWNTIME ===
- after 1h: Okafor stands in front of Kit waiting for an answer that mostly comes as a shrug and another sip; she calls it dereliction of duty in a voice like a signed form, then goes back to ops to draft answers to questions Earth hasn't asked yet.
- after 3h: Teo, refusing to accept the empty spares racks, starts cutting and shaping a seal from a spare glove gasket and RTV at the galley table, measuring the old impeller by hand, hands shaking every time the nineteen on the board catches his eye.
- after 6h: Priya catches Lev's headlamp glow through the lab curtain and finds him logging nothing, and when she teases him about vampire hours he jokes about his cultures being light-sensitive, which is not quite a lie.
- after 9h: The fifth mug goes down half-finished; Kit's hands stop cooperating before the rest of them does, and the bench turns out not to be a commitment after all.

=== ALSO DURING THE DOWNTIME ===
- (heard from elsewhere; only a sound, call or message reaches the player) Teo hand-shapes a substitute impeller seal from a glove gasket and adhesive, and reports it might hold if it cures overnight — the first real path back to water, untested.

=== WHAT ENDS IT ===
Kit Navarro blacks out from exhaustion and goes down hard against a bulkhead.

=== WHERE EVERYONE IS WHEN IT HITS ===
- Dr. Imani Okafor: in Ops & Comms, Drafting answers to Mission Control's inevitable questions, with Kit's silence filed under problems to solve
- Dr. Lev Sorensen: in Lab, Working by headlamp on the unlogged cultures, checking them by hand in the cold
- Priya Raman: in Suit Room & Airlock, Suit maintenance by emergency strips, keeping her hands busy and her eyes on the tally board
- Teo Bauer: in Commons, Fitting his improvised seal to the stripped impeller, talking himself through it out loud

=== WORN PHRASES (recent scenes keep using these: do not use them or close variants) ===
- "charging circuit is clean"
- "your hands are steady"
- "the ration bar still"

=== TASK ===
Write 3 or 4 beats in second person ("you" is Kit Navarro), 250–350 words in total. Start each beat on its own line with a time marker since the downtime began: [+0h], [+6h], [+15h] and so on.
1. The first beats are a brief montage of the downtime, starting after the last scene (never retell it), a few sentences each: how the days pass, how people get along, the small things. Kit Navarro does only what their plan says and treats people according to the feelings in STATUS; others deal with whatever comes up.
2. The final beat starts with [+9h] and is a live scene in present tense: the thing that ends the downtime hits Commons, and the people there react in their own voices.
Hard rules:
- Use each character's pronouns exactly as given in STATUS.
- Do not reveal anyone's secrets unless the montage above says it came out.
- No big decisions for Kit Navarro. End the final beat on a moment that demands the player's response; the last paragraph is never Kit Navarro's own line or action.
Reply with the beats only.

response.text:
[+1h] Okafor stands over you waiting for an answer. You give her a shrug and another sip, which is the honest version. She calls it dereliction of duty in a voice like a signed form and goes back to ops to draft answers Earth hasn't asked yet. You don't blame her. That's the worst part.

[+3h] Teo takes over the galley table, cutting a seal out of a glove gasket with a scraper and RTV, measuring the old impeller by hand. His hands shake every time his eyes catch the nineteen on the board. You drink. He doesn't look at you, and you don't make him.

[+6h] Priya catches the headlamp glow through the lab curtain and teases Lev about vampire hours. He jokes back about light-sensitive cultures, which is not quite a lie, and she lets it go with a look you file away. She chalks the power tally again. Same numbers. She frowns at them like they might blink first.

[+9h] The fifth mug goes down half-finished and your hands stop cooperating before the rest of you does. The bench, it turns out, was never a commitment.

Teo is at the stripped impeller housing, fitting his homemade seal, talking himself through it — "seat it square, square, come on" — when your shoulder finds the bulkhead. The deck comes up fast. There's a clatter, a mug rolling its last circle somewhere by your ear, and the cold of the floor plate through your shirt.

"Kit — hey, hey." Teo's boots skid; he's on his knees next to you, freckles bloodless. "Priya! MED! Somebody—" His voice cracks. "Okay, okay, you're okay, you just went down, you just—" He grabs your wrist, checking your pulse like Lev showed him, badly. "Don't do this. Don't you dare do this."

From the lab curtain, Lev's headlamp swings toward the noise.

Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.

- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===

- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface) [region: station]
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage) [region: crater-rim]

Chapter 0 — Before the story: Sol 1: The Ares crew landed on the rim of Hellas and sealed the first module of Ares Deep. Sol 120: A regional dust storm buried the solar field for nine sols; the crew lived on batteries and rationed heat until it cleared. Sol 190: Mission Control confirmed that the next cargo lander had launched from Earth.
Chapter 1 — Rust Sky, Draining Reserve: A regional dust storm bore down on Ares Deep, and Teo went out alone into its leading edge to finish Kit's array tie-downs, taking a fall on the icy anchor line that injured his shoulder. As the storm buried the sun and the station dropped to battery reserve, Okafor found the reserve draining four percent an hour and demanded answers. Teo deflected with a too-cheerful sensor-fault theory, but Kit knew the rattle in the recycler had started six nights earlier, on the night of Teo's late hydroponics shift.
Chapter 2 — Dark Water: Exhausted and unfed, Kit blacked out against a bulkhead in commons while the dust storm swallowed the solar field. Priya hauled Teo to med bay for his storm-fall shoulder, but the worse blow came when the water recycler ground to a halt and Teo admitted the impeller had seized — never the sensor fault he'd claimed. Lev taped Kit's hip, issued warnings about food and caffeine, and vanished back to his lab without checking on anyone else, leaving Kit to tally what stored water meant with the sky still rust-dark.

When Kit collapsed earlier from exhaustion and had stayed silent about the recycler and Teo, Okafor confronted them in commons about sitting out the emergencies.

Teo then freed the recycler's seized impeller enough to hand-turn it, reporting flow could return within a sol if he found a replacement seal.
Chapter 6 — Emergency Strips: Okafor transmitted the emergency power report to Mission Control and posted its summary on the galley board, then publicly confronted Kit over watching the failing recycler for six nights without reporting it. - [T2] Teo went out alone into the storm's leading edge to secure Kit's tie-downs, got the last array half-cinched, and took a fall on the icy anchor line.
- [T3] Kit Navarro collapsed against a bulkhead in commons from exhaustion and hunger.

- [T4] Teo admitted the recycler's impeller seized and that it was never a sensor fault.
- [T5] Okafor runs the water inventory herself while everyone else stands frozen; the count comes back worse than it should be — Teo's over-cycles bled the reserve for six nights — putting stored water at roughly nineteen…
- [T7] Lev showed Kit readings from an unlogged incubator and asked for a second opinion before telling anyone else.
- [T8] The battery reserve crosses its critical floor and the station's load-shedding kicks in automatically — heat to the far modules cuts out first, then the lab incubators, and the galley lights die to emergency strips.
- [T8] The battery reserve crossed its critical floor and load-shedding cut heat to the far modules, lab incubator power and galley lighting.
- [T9] Halvorsen Aerospace's quarterly review comes over the uplink: the board praises the crew and asks for more footage for its publicity campaign.
- [T9] Okafor and Teo triage the load-shedding without Kit: Teo drags insulation and heat blankets onto the seedling racks while Okafor kills every discretionary circuit herself.
- [T11] Okafor transmits the emergency power report to Mission Control, documenting the load-shedding, the seized recycler impeller and the battery reserve, then posts the sent message summary on the galley board for the crew…
- [T13] Lev and Teo work by emergency light in the lab and hydroponics to salvage what they can from the dead incubators, and Lev reports to the crew that the ice cultures are lost but the seedling racks under their blanket…
- [T13] Okafor sends Mission Control the daily status update including the crew collapse, and the 14-minute silence afterward feels heavier than usual.
- [T13] Lev and Teo salvaged the dead incubators overnight; the ice cultures are lost but the blanket-wrapped seedlings are holding.
- [T13] Lev quietly began checking the archive vials one by one to see if any survived the cold.
- [T13] Kit was ordered horizontal in med bay and given electrolytes after the scanner flagged dehydration and exhaustion.

Priya is in the galley doorway with two heat packs and a face that says she's been watching you breathe. "Crew watchfulness," she says, before you can ask. "Standard procedure. I made it up just now." She sits down across from you and puts a heat pack in your hands, closing your fingers around it. "Teo's asleep, Okafor's buried in ops, Lev's in the lab with his vials. It's just us." Her voice drops. "So. Six nights, Kit. You knew the recycler was dying and you said nothing. I'm not Mission Control. I'm not going to log it. I just want to know why."

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

- The Ares program: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom) [region: station]
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]

- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage) [region: crater-rim]

=== REGIONS ===
- station: Ares Deep — The outpost itself: pressurized modules dug into the rim, run day to day by the crew and on paper by Mission Control. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- crater-rim: Hellas crater rim — Broken slopes around the outpost: the solar field, the ice drill site and the rover tracks. Suits required; dust devils and slope failures are common. (neighbours: station, basin-floor, relay-mast)
- basin-floor: Hellas basin floor — The deepest plain on Mars, kilometres below the rim. Thicker air, colder nights, and supply drops land there when they miss. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- relay-mast: Relay mast — An automated Halvorsen relay and weather station a day's drive along the rim, the nearest other built thing on the planet. (neighbours: crater-rim)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== WORLD LORE ===
- The Ares program: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

request.system:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom) [region: station]
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface) [region: station]
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage) [region: crater-rim]

=== REGIONS ===
- station: Ares Deep — The outpost itself: pressurized modules dug into the rim, run day to day by the crew and on paper by Mission Control. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- crater-rim: Hellas crater rim — Broken slopes around the outpost: the solar field, the ice drill site and the rover tracks. Suits required; dust devils and slope failures are common. (neighbours: station, basin-floor, relay-mast)
- basin-floor: Hellas basin floor — The deepest plain on Mars, kilometres below the rim. Thicker air, colder nights, and supply drops land there when they miss. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- relay-mast: Relay mast — An automated Halvorsen relay and weather station a day's drive along the rim, the nearest other built thing on the planet. (neighbours: crater-rim)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== WORLD LORE ===
- The Ares program: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
- sorensen: Dr. Lev Sorensen (he/him), medic and astrobiologist, 39. Traits: curious, secretive, gentle. Wants: be the first person to confirm life on Mars. Voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
- raman: Priya Raman (she/her), pilot and rover technician, 31. Traits: warm, impatient, fiercely loyal. Wants: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday. Voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
- bauer: Teo Bauer (he/him), hydroponics technician, 24. Traits: eager, anxious, people-pleaser. Wants: prove he belongs on this crew. Voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.

=== STORY SO FAR ===
Chapter 0 — Before the story: Sol 1: The Ares crew landed on the rim of Hellas and sealed the first module of Ares Deep. Sol 120: A regional dust storm buried the solar field for nine sols; the crew lived on batteries and rationed heat until it cleared. Sol 190: Mission Control confirmed that the next cargo lander had launched from Earth.
Chapter 1 — Rust Sky, Draining Reserve: A regional dust storm bore down on Ares Deep, and Teo went out alone into its leading edge to finish Kit's array tie-downs, taking a fall on the icy anchor line that injured his shoulder. As the storm buried the sun and the station dropped to battery reserve, Okafor found the reserve draining four percent an hour and demanded answers. Teo deflected with a too-cheerful sensor-fault theory, but Kit knew the rattle in the recycler had started six nights earlier, on the night of Teo's late hydroponics shift.
Chapter 2 — Dark Water: Exhausted and unfed, Kit blacked out against a bulkhead in commons while the dust storm swallowed the solar field. Priya hauled Teo to med bay for his storm-fall shoulder, but the worse blow came when the water recycler ground to a halt and Teo admitted the impeller had seized — never the sensor fault he'd claimed. Lev taped Kit's hip, issued warnings about food and caffeine, and vanished back to his lab without checking on anyone else, leaving Kit to tally what stored water meant with the sky still rust-dark.
Chapter 3 — Nineteen Sols: Okafor ran the water inventory herself and found Teo's over-cycles had bled the reserve down to nineteen sols, posting the number on the galley board without explaining the shortfall before shutting herself in ops to decide what to tell Earth. Lev asked through the lab curtain that his water allocation stay unchanged, while Priya casually sounded Kit out on how Okafor was holding up. When Kit collapsed earlier from exhaustion and had stayed silent about the recycler and Teo, Okafor confronted them in commons about sitting out the emergencies.
Chapter 4 — Emergency Strips: Lev came to Kit privately with readings from an unlogged incubator, asking for a second opinion before telling anyone else. Before Kit could sit with it, the battery reserve crossed its critical floor and load-shedding cut heat to the far modules, killed the lab incubators, and dropped the galley to emergency strips — with Priya confirming to Okafor that the drain was coming from inside the station. Okafor demanded Kit set the station's load priorities, while Teo spent the night in hydroponics culling crops that couldn't survive rationing and Lev reacted with alarm at losing his incubators.
Chapter 5 — Emergency Strips: As Halvorsen's quarterly review praised the crew and asked for more publicity footage, Okafor and Teo triaged the load-shedding without Kit, killing discretionary circuits and blanketing the seedling racks while Priya confirmed the power drain was internal. Kit, running on fumes, blacked out hard against a bulkhead. Teo then freed the recycler's seized impeller enough to hand-turn it, reporting flow could return within a sol if he found a replacement seal.
Chapter 6 — Emergency Strips: Okafor transmitted the emergency power report to Mission Control and posted its summary on the galley board, then publicly confronted Kit over watching the failing recycler for six nights without reporting it. Teo searched every spares rack and found no replacement impeller seal anywhere on the station. Running on fumes, Kit blacked out and went down hard against a bulkhead.
Chapter 7 — Nineteen Sols and a Cold Dark: While Kit lay ordered horizontal in med bay on electrolytes, Lev and Teo salvaged the dead incubators by emergency light, saving the blanket-wrapped seedlings but losing the ice cultures, and Lev quietly began checking the archive vials for survivors. Okafor sent Mission Control the status update including Kit's collapse, and the fourteen-minute silence felt heavier than usual. Teo hand-turned the rebuilt impeller to report thin but real flow, pending a replacement seal that didn't exist on station.
Chapter 8 — Emergency Strips and a Long Night: Kit broke down crying in med bay from exhaustion, and Lev warned that one more coffee pouch could have caused cardiac arrhythmia, strapping on a heart monitor while Mission Control demanded a formal medical status report within the sol. Priya quietly checked on Kit after the second blackout, framing it as crew watchfulness. Teo spent the whole night hand-turning the recycler impeller, reporting thin but steady flow before falling asleep against the housing, and Lev filed Kit's medical report to Mission Control, whose acknowledgment arrived with daily updates attached.
Chapter 9 — Rhythm and Rations: As the storm thinned and Priya promised the batteries could come off the critical floor, Kit's exhaustion finally broke them — a hidden coffee pouch, a logged violation, and a cardiac arrhythmia that dropped them in commons while Lev called the rhythm and Priya held them down. Lev declared Kit a supply problem and put Priya on the med bay inventory, while Okafor rebuilt the six-night recycler log gap in ops knowing Mission Control would ask who knew what and when. Through it all, Teo kept hand-turning the impeller past midnight on fumes.
Chapter 10 — Salt and Seals: Kit kept running on salt pouches after Lev quietly removed the emergency coffee kit, blacking out hard against a bulkhead and breaking down under the strain while Teo hand-turned the recycler impeller through the night and Okafor rebuilt the six-night log gap alone in ops. Priya covered the sleeping Teo with a thermal blanket and pleaded with Kit to rest. request.system:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom) [region: station]
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons) [region: station]
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface) [region: station]
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface) [region: station]
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage) [region: crater-rim]

=== REGIONS ===
- station: Ares Deep — The outpost itself: pressurized modules dug into the rim, run day to day by the crew and on paper by Mission Control. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- crater-rim: Hellas crater rim — Broken slopes around the outpost: the solar field, the ice drill site and the rover tracks. Suits required; dust devils and slope failures are common. (neighbours: station, basin-floor, relay-mast)
- basin-floor: Hellas basin floor — The deepest plain on Mars, kilometres below the rim. Thicker air, colder nights, and supply drops land there when they miss. (neighbours: crater-rim)
- relay-mast: Relay mast — An automated Halvorsen relay and weather station a day's drive along the rim, the nearest other built thing on the planet. (neighbours: crater-rim)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== WORLD LORE ===
- The Ares program: Ares Deep is the first long-stay crewed outpost on Mars. An international space agency runs it through Mission Control, and Halvorsen Aerospace pays most of the bills in exchange for the publicity. Crews serve 500-sol rotations, and nobody has yet promised a second crew.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.

Chapter 0 — Before the story: Sol 1: The Ares crew landed on the rim of Hellas and sealed the first module of Ares Deep. Lev taped Kit's hip, issued warnings about food and caffeine, and vanished back to his lab without checking on anyone else, leaving Kit to tally what stored water meant with the sky still rust-dark.
Chapter 3 — Nineteen Sols: Okafor ran the water inventory herself and found Teo's over-cycles had bled the reserve down to nineteen sols, posting the number on the galley board without explaining the shortfall before shutting herself in ops to decide what to tell Earth. Lev asked through the lab curtain that his water allocation stay unchanged, while Priya casually sounded Kit out on how Okafor was holding up. When Kit collapsed earlier from exhaustion and had stayed silent about the recycler and Teo, Okafor confronted them in commons about sitting out the emergencies.
